Hi Eli — Ben here (Billing Ops). We pulled the exports you requested. Summary of preliminary findings:

1) What we observed
- Our attribution exporter shows ~4.9M tokens attributed to DatumHealth across May 1–7. Your expected volume is ~3.1M; delta ~1.8M tokens (the ~$12.8k overage).
- The delta clusters in short bursts (sub-minute) around UTC 2026-05-03T02:10–02:14 and 2026-05-05T19:42–19:47.

2) Root-cause hypothesis (engineering confirmed)
- We have a rolling-window attribution edge-case that affected clients using long-lived streaming connections combined with periodic background prefetch jobs. The sampler counts certain prefetch frames as \"client-initiated\" when a transport alias header (x-rw-client-id) is reused across a connection handoff. In short: two independent internal events (background syncs + keepalive handoffs) caused the same session id to be scored twice across different shards.
- This is not a customer-side code issue; it's a server-side attribution mismatch inside our rolling-window sampler logic.

3) Evidence attached
- redwood_usage_window_report_may1-7.csv (per-session export showing token counts per session id and timestamps).
- sampling_snippet.txt (3-line excerpt showing duplicate attribution lines for the same session id around 2026-05-03T02:12:18Z).

4) Proposed remediation and commercial offer
- Immediate one-time credit for the full overage while we perform an internal audit (we will reverse if audit shows otherwise).
- Engineering fix scheduled: patch to rolling-window sampler to ignore prefetch frames when x-rw-client-id handoff occurs; target deployment: 2026-05-20.
- Post-fix, we'll run a backfill to ensure no residual double-counting in downstream billing exports.

If that approach works for you, I can generate a credit memo and route to Procurement. We can also provide token-level evidence for the two burst windows; tell me if you want the full compressed logs.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Billing Operations Lead, Redwood Inference
